A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same backchannel/filler representation study. All 30 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable; corresponding methods, results, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, embedding analyses, dialogue-generation results, and MapTask dialogue-act classification results in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds analyses across hidden layers, bootstrap estimates, and additional qualitative dialogue examples.

M1.justification: The MASK, NTP, and TurnGPT-based TTP objectives, model families, and core embedding-pooling/PCA/clustering pipeline remain unchanged. V2's explicit special-token explanation matches preprocessing already documented in v1 Appendix B and Figure 6. Additional layer probes extend the analysis rather than introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both use English Switchboard and MapTask and Japanese BTSJ data. Representation analysis, dialogue continuation, and MapTask dialogue-act classification are retained. Additional layer probes and qualitative examples remain within this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Clustering retains BERT, GPT-2/TurnGPT, LLaMA-3, and Qwen-3 comparisons; NLG retains LLaMA-3, Qwen-3, and GPT-2; dialogue-act classification retains all four model families. Contrastive learning remains discussed but unevaluated.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces v1's general 80/20 split description with 80/20 for MASK/NTP and a separate training/validation/testing partition for TTP. Appendix C changes TurnGPT batch size from 3 to 4, dropout from 0.1 to 0.3, and learning rate from 0.0001 to 0.0005. V2 also specifies selected layers for the new analysis. These reported changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analysis across selected hidden layers for all four model families under no-context and one-context settings (Appendix D.1, Figures 7–8), addressing an investigation left for future work in v1. It also expands the qualitative generation analysis from four to six examples.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates. V2 introduces 1,000-resample bootstrap estimation with 95% confidence-interval half-widths for silhouette scores (Table 6), and adds ± quantities for NLG perplexity, BERTScore, and BLEU (Tables 4–5). The NLG uncertainty quantities are not defined, and additional training runs are not established.

E6.justification: BERT clustering results are substantially revised: English no-context, 100-dimensional pre-/post-fine-tuning silhouette averages change from 0.191/0.192 in v1 Table 9 to 0.141/0.233 in v2 Table 10. Japanese BERT scores and both BERT cluster-count tables also change. V2 adds layer-dependent findings and qualitative examples, and revises visual findings. NLG point estimates, dialogue-act accuracies, and the other models' existing clustering tables are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of MASK, NTP, TTP, silhouette scores, and NLG perplexity are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims that fine-tuning improves backchannel/filler representations and produces dialogue closer to human utterances. Revised research-question wording and additional supporting analyses do not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of representation changes across layers and claims that the additional dialogue examples demonstrate pragmatic differentiation and appropriate omission of fillers. Its t-SNE discussion replaces the earlier LLaMA pretraining explanation with an unresolved BERT separation anomaly. General-capacity side effects are described as minor instead of almost absent; large-scale human evaluation remains a limitation.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies project code/data access links and a Zenodo archive in Supplementary Material. Appendix C revises the documented TurnGPT hyperparameters, while GPU resources, runtimes, and LoRA configuration remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Edlund et al. (2008), Efron (1992), Stolcke et al. (2000), and van der Lee et al. (2021), and removes Hough et al. (2015) and the standalone Jucker (1998) reference. The main research positioning and contrastive-learning discussion remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction, and numerous passages, replaces the opening dialogue with a corpus excerpt, and renames Background to Related Work. Appendix D is reorganized, including separating the existing NLG metric explanations into their own subsection. The overall main-text outline and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, t-SNE displays are extensively reworked, central summary plots are enlarged, and appendix tables and figures are regrouped. Distance heatmaps adopt common 0–100 colorbars. New layer plots and bootstrap Table 6 are added; the Japanese Qwen comparison from v1 Figure 22 is redrawn and promoted to v2 Figure 5.

improvement.justification: V2 partly addresses v1's last-layer-only limitation, makes the Japanese BERT averages agree with their table entries, and adds code/data access instructions and clearer central figures. These support a limited quality gain. New uncertainty reporting remains imperfect: the English BERT one-context fine-tuned mean is 0.391 in bootstrap Table 6 versus 0.178 in Table 10 without reconciliation, and the NLG ± quantities are undefined.
